According to recent reports, barcode regions from the input reference and screened plasmid pools were PCR-amplified and indexed using the Nextera XT Index Kit v2 Set A (Illumina, FC-131-2001). Primers used for NGS are provided in Supplementary Table 5. Indexed amplicons were sequenced on an in-house MiSeq instrument. Activity and specificity scores for each design were calculated using an Enrich2-based pipeline23,46 on a log2-fold change basis and normalized to the score of TnsAWT.

E. coli cells that had undergone in vivo transposition assays were plated on agar containing 100 µg ml−1 carbenicillin, 50 µg ml−1 kanamycin and 30 µg ml−1 chloramphenicol to select for all integration events. More than 1,000 colonies were scraped for gDNA extraction using the Wizard Genomic DNA Purification Kit (Promega, A1125). Tagmentation-based transposon insertion sequencing (TagTn-seq)11 was performed on the extracted gDNA. Libraries were prepared by fragmenting gDNA with the Nextera XT DNA Library Kit (Illumina, FC-131-1024), followed by PCR amplification using an i7 primer and VchCAST right-end (RE)-specific primers, and indexing prior to sequencing on the in-house MiSeq. Reads mapping to the intact VchCAST pDonor were filtered from the resulting sequencing data using BBMap (v39.80), and RE-adjacent sequences were mapped to the cJP003 genome to profile integration site distribution.

TnsA activity is assessed through the formation of simple insertion products, as TnsA-mediated DNA cleavage results in cleavage of the 5′ end of donor DNA and lack of cleavage results in integration of the donor DNA backbone, otherwise referred to as co-integrates. We used long-read sequencing to distinguish between these two products, as previously established8.

Sources indicate that E. coli cells that had undergone in vivo transposition assays were plated on agar containing 100 µg ml−1 carbenicillin, 50 µg ml−1 kanamycin, 30 µg ml−1 chloramphenicol, and 0.1% (w/v) l-arabinose to select specifically for on-target integration events. More than 1,000 colonies were scraped and gDNA was extracted using the Wizard Genomic DNA Purification Kit (ProMega, A1125). Whole-genome sequencing was performed by Plasmidsaurus. Sequencing reads were analysed to identify integration products by detecting reads containing both target-site and left-end (LE) sequences, which define the boundaries of the integrated region. Reads containing pDonor backbone sequence were classified as co-integrates, while reads lacking pDonor backbone but containing the downstream target-site sequence were classified as simple insertions. Reads lacking both features were classified as ambiguous.

According to recent reports, far-UV circular dichroism spectra were collected using a JASCO CD spectropolarimeter. WT-TnsA and D1A were buffer exchanged into 10 mM potassium phosphate (pH 7.4) and analysed at a final concentration of 15 µM using a 0.1 cm path length quartz cuvette. Spectra were recorded from 195 to 280 nm at room temperature in continuous scanning mode with a 1.0 nm bandwidth and a scan speed of 200 nm min−1. Eight accumulations were collected for each sample and averaged to improve the signal-to-noise ratio. A buffer-only spectrum was recorded under identical conditions and subtracted from each protein spectrum.

The corrected circular dichroism signal was converted to mean residue ellipticity according to the manufacturer’s instructions:.

Recent findings suggest that where θobs is the buffer-subtracted ellipticity, n is the number of amino acid residues, c is the protein concentration (M), and l is the cuvette path length (cm). WT-TnsA and D1A were normalized using 229 and 236 amino acid residues, respectively. For plotting, mean residue ellipticity values were divided by 1,000 and are reported as [θ] ×10−3 (deg cm2 dmol−1).

According to recent reports, the DNA substrate used was designed based on in vivo genomic profiling experiments, synthesized as single-stranded DNA, and annealed to form a strand-transfer product substrate which was used for complex reconstitution, following our previously described strategy12,13. The left end spans LE1 through LE3 (positions 1–109) and the right end spans RE1 through RE3 (1–72), as shown in Supplementary Fig. 4. The native arrangement of left and right ends are identical up to position 30 (encompassing the 8 bp terminal sequence and LE1/ RE1). Past the first binding site, the placement and spacing of LE2–LE3 and RE2–RE3 differ, additionally there is a IHF binding site between LE1 and LE2 (Supplementary Fig. 4).

According to recent reports, two double-stranded DNA substrates were independently assembled for the STC and transpososome reconstitution: a LE fragment and a RE fragment, each designed to recapitulate the relevant structural elements of the VchCAST RNA-guided transposition product, including the transposon terminal repeat sequences, the 5 bp target site duplication, and flanking target and gDNA regions (Supplementary Table 6). A diagram of the substrates can be found in Supplementary Fig. 4.

The LE fragment was assembled from three oligonucleotides: LE–TGS, which contains the transposon LE and flanking gDNA, Target-RC, which completes the double-stranded target genomic region, and LE–HFR, which provides the complementary LE region to LE–TGS along with a host flanking region for TnsA binding.

The RE fragment was assembled from four oligonucleotides: RE–TGS, which contains the RE and the target strand for guide RNA binding, NTGS–Scramble, a non-target strand oligonucleotide contained a scrambled sequence to facilitate bubble formation, RE–HFR, an oligonucleotide that complements the RE sequence of RE–TGS and contains a flanking HFR region, and DTB–LUEGO, a desthiobiotinylated oligonucleotide incorporated at the 5′ end of the RE fragment to enable streptavidin-based affinity capture of the assembled complexes during pull-down experiments47.

It has been revealed that prior to annealing, all oligonucleotides were purified by HPLC using an Agilent 1260 Infinity II system equipped with an AdvanceBio Oligonucleotide column (Agilent Technologies) to ensure incorporation of only full-length species. The LE and RE fragments were each assembled independently by combining their respective oligonucleotides at equimolar concentrations in annealing buffer (10 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5, 50 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA), heating to 95 °C for 5 min, and gradually cooling to 50 °C at 1 °C per min using a thermal cycler (Bio-Rad). The annealed fragments were stored separately until used in STC and transpososome reconstitutions.

STC assembly reactions were prepared using an annealed DNA substrate (0.5 µM in 100 µl) and containing TnsB together with D1A using the same 1:5:10 stoichiometry. Complex assembly was initially carried out under high-salt conditions in a buffer containing 26 mM HEPES (pH 7.5), 5 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.5), 20 mM KCl, 750 mM NaCl, 0.2 mM MgCl2, 15 mM magnesium acetate, 2% glycerol, 1 mM DTT and 0.1% Tween-20. Following assembly, samples were dialysed overnight at 4 °C from high-salt buffer into an identical low-salt buffer in which the NaCl concentration was reduced to 150 mM to promote stable complex formation.

For affinity capture of assembled complexes, Streptavidin Mag Sepharose magnetic beads (Cytiva) were washed 3 times with 500 μl of low-salt buffer prior to use. Dialysed samples were incubated with the equilibrated streptavidin beads for 1 h at room temperature with continuous rotation to allow binding of biotinylated DNA substrates and associated protein complexes.

Following incubation, the beads were washed 3 times with 500 μl of low-salt buffer to remove unbound proteins and nonspecific material. Bound complexes were subsequently eluted using low-salt buffer supplemented with 10 mM biotin. Elution was performed in 2 sequential rounds using 50 µl buffer per step, with each incubation carried out for 30 min at room temperature under rotation before collection of the eluate. Elution fractions were analysed by SDS–PAGE to confirm the presence of protein components within the assembled complexes. Sample quality, homogeneity and the presence of assembled STCs were further evaluated by negative-stain electron microscopy prior to cryo-EM grid preparation and vitrification.

Sequential on-bead assembly of the HIC was performed by first capturing the desthiobiotinylated RE substrate (0.5 µM in 100 µl) on Streptavidin Mag Sepharose magnetic beads (Cytiva). Binding was carried out for 1 h at room temperature with gentle rotation in binding buffer comprising 26 mM HEPES (pH 7.5), 5 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.5), 20 mM KCl, 750 mM NaCl, 0.2 mM MgCl2, 15 mM MgOAc, 2% glycerol, 1 mM ATP, 1 mM DTT, and 0.1% Tween-20, followed by 3 washes with 500 µl of the same buffer.

Industry observers note that cascade–TniQ was subsequently introduced at a 1:2 DNA:protein molar ratio and incubated for 1 h at room temperature, followed by 3 washes. The LE substrate (0.5 µM), pre-complexed with E. coli IHF at a 1:8 DNA-to-protein molar ratio, was then added alongside TnsB (1:5 DNA:protein) and designed TnsA (1:10 DNA:protein), and the assembly was allowed to proceed for 1 h at room temperature. Beads were washed 3 times with 500 µl binding buffer. In the final step, TnsC was introduced at a 1:10 DNA-to-protein ratio in binding buffer supplemented with equimolar concentrations of ATP and ATPγS (1 mM each) and incubated for 1 h at room temperature. Unbound proteins were removed by 3 washes with 500 µl of ATP/ATPγS-containing binding buffer.

The assembled HIC was released from the beads by two sequential elution steps, each using 50 µl of elution buffer (binding buffer supplemented with 10 mM biotin) incubated under rotation for 30 min. Eluted fractions were resolved by SDS–PAGE to verify the presence of all HIC components. Prior to cryo-EM grid preparation, samples were evaluated by negative-stain electron microscopy to confirm the presence of assembled HIC particles and to assess sample homogeneity.

According to recent reports, graphene sheets with a poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) support layer (ACS Material, TTG100BB,25 ×25 mm) were stored at 4 °C until use. Graphene transfer onto cryo-EM grids was performed based on a previously described protocol with minor modifications48. Ultrafoil grids (Au R1.2/1.3, Quantifoil) were placed on a 3D-printed grid transfer tool immersed in deionized water. Excess support material from the graphene pad was trimmed, and the PMMA/graphene pad was placed gently onto the water surface to avoid overflow onto the graphene layer. After positioning, the water level was gradually lowered by syringe withdrawal, allowing the graphene sheet to settle onto the grids. Grids were left overnight at room temperature to anneal, then baked at 150 °C for 30 min to promote firm adhesion. Grids were transferred to a Petri dish, and PMMA was removed by three successive acetone washes. Graphene-coated grids were individually transferred to a grid box and stored at room temperature until use.

STC samples were prepared for cryo-EM either directly from pull-down elution fractions or following two- to four-fold dilution in low-salt buffer. Graphene-coated grids were prepared as described above. Prior to sample application, grids were plasma-cleaned using a Solarus II Plasma Cleaner (Gatan) under an Ar/O2 atmosphere at 10 W for 10 s (s), with the graphene-coated surface oriented upward.

According to recent reports, for vitrification, 4 µl of STC sample was applied to the carbon side of a graphene-coated grid and incubated for 60 s inside a Vitrobot Mark IV chamber (Thermo Fisher Scientific) maintained at 4 °C and 100% relative humidity. Grids were blotted for 3.5 s at a blot force of −7 and immediately plunge-frozen into liquid ethane cooled by liquid nitrogen.

HIC samples were prepared for cryo-EM from either undiluted pull-down eluates or two- to four-fold dilutions thereof. Graphene-coated grids were prepared as described above and plasma-cleaned using a Solarus II Plasma Cleaner (Gatan) under an Ar/O2 atmosphere at 10 W for 10 s with the graphene-coated face oriented upward.

Sources indicate that for vitrification, 4 µl of HIC sample was applied to the carbon side of a graphene-coated grid and incubated for 60 s inside a Vitrobot Mark IV chamber at 4 °C and 100% relative humidity. Grids were blotted for 3.5 s at a blot force of −7 before plunge-freezing into liquid ethane cooled by liquid nitrogen.

According to recent reports, ni-NTA affinity grids were prepared as previously described49. Quantifoil Au R1.2/1.3 grids were coated with a Ni-NTA lipid monolayer composed of 20% 18:1 DGS-NTA(Ni) (Avanti Polar Lipids) diluted with DOPC (18:1; Avanti Polar Lipids). Grids were incubated with 3 µl of His-tagged HIC diluted in 2 µl of elution buffer (26 mM HEPES pH 7.5, 5 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5, 20 mM KCl, 750 mM NaCl, 0.2 mM MgCl2, 15 mM MgOAc, 2% glycerol, 1 mM ATP, 1 mM DTT, 0.1% Tween-20) for 1 h at 4 °C in a humidity chamber to allow affinity capture. Unbound material was removed by three brief washes with elution buffer, after which grids were blotted and plunge-frozen in liquid ethane using a Vitrobot operated at 4 °C and 100% relative humidity with a blot force of −7 and blot time of 3.5 s.

According to recent reports, vitrified STC samples were initially screened on a Talos Arctica transmission electron microscope (Thermo Fisher Scientific) operated with fringe-free illumination at 130,000× magnification (0.63 Å per pixel) and 200 kV, equipped with a Gatan K3 direct electron detector and a BioQuantum imaging filter (20 eV slit width). Data were collected using the EPU software package (Thermo Fisher Scientific). This screening step was used to assess grid quality and particle distribution prior to large-scale data collection. Grids of sufficient quality were subsequently imaged on a Titan Krios G3i transmission electron microscope (Thermo Fisher Scientific) operated with fringe-free illumination at 130,000× magnification (0.745 Å per pixel) and 300 kV, equipped with a Falcon 4i (4k × 4k) direct electron detector, a BioQuantum imaging filter, and a 20 eV energy-selecting slit. Data collection employed the aberration-free image shift and multi-shot-per-hole acquisition modes of EPU. For the STC dataset, 7,724 movies were collected using EPU with image shift, with nominal defocus ranging from −1.5 to −2.5 µm at 0.2 µm intervals. Each movie was acquired with a 3.1 s exposure and a total dose of 60 e− Å−2, fractionated into 60 frames. Frames were aligned using MotionCor250, and CTF estimation was performed in cryoSPARC v4.7.151. The full data processing workflow is presented in Supplementary Fig. 4.

Recent findings suggest that particles were initially picked using blob picker, and approximately 290,000 extracted particles were subjected to 2D classification. Classes representing the STC were identified and used as templates for a second round of template-based particle picking, yielding approximately 1,000,000 particles that were re-subjected to 2D classification. The resulting 22,000 particles were used to train a Topaz neural network picking model (v0.2.5)52. After confirming model performance, additional particles were extracted from all micrographs using the trained model. The latest particle set underwent 2D classification, and selection of high-quality classes yielded 97,972 particles that were used for ab initio reconstruction. Heterogeneous refinement separated the dataset into two classes: 70,006 particles representing the STC complex and the remainder classified as non-particles. Non-uniform refinement of the STC class produced an initial map at 2.9 Å resolution. The particle stack was then subjected to 3D classification using principal component analysis with a 13 Å resolution cut-off, separating 18,831 particles lacking target DNA from 51,169 particles with target DNA bound. Both subsets were independently subjected to non-uniform refinement, yielding a 3.2 Å map for the STC without target DNA and a 2.9 Å map for the STC with target DNA. Both maps were further processed with DeepEMhancer v12132253 prior to model building.

Initial cryo-EM data collection on graphene grids revealed a strong preferred orientation bias, limiting the angular coverage of the dataset. To improve particle orientation distribution and enable higher-quality three-dimensional reconstructions, Ni-NTA lipid monolayer grids were subsequently prepared49.

Recent findings suggest that A total of 144,294 movies were collected at a pixel size of 0.848 Å and processed using Patch Motion Correction and Patch CTF Estimation with a CTF-fit cut-off of less than 10 Å. Initial particle picking was performed by blob picking on approximately 2,600 micrographs, yielding ~570,000 extracted particles (binned 3×), which were subjected to two rounds of 2D classification to generate ~5,000 representative particles for training a Topaz neural network picking model (v0.2.5)52. The trained model was applied across all ~22,000 micrographs, extracting 2,722,447 particles (binned 3×). Following two rounds of 2D classification, 897,848 particles were retained for further analysis. The complete data processing workflow is described in Extended Data Fig. 4.

According to recent reports, single-particle analysis revealed substantial compositional heterogeneity within the reconstituted sample. Two-dimensional class averages resolved density for all expected components in multiple orientations (Extended Data Fig. 4). Heterogeneous refinement (n = 4) partitioned the dataset into 4 populations: 2 HIC classes (131,242 particles, 14.6%; and 462,255 particles, 54.8%), 1 STC–TnsC class (127,845 particles, 14.2%) and 1 Cascade class (146,705 particles, 16.4%). These populations enabled classification of the following assemblies: a Cascade–TniQ sub-complex (3.3 Å), a STC (2.9 Å) an STC–TnsC assembly (4.3 Å) and the complete HIC (4.5 Å) (Extended Data Fig. 4). Each population was further processed by sub-classification and homogeneous refinement. For the HIC, signal subtraction of the STC–TnsC region followed by 2D slice projection-guided particle sorting enabled focused local refinement, yielding a map at 4.5 Å resolution (Fourier shell correlation (FSC) = 0.143). Non-uniform refinement of the Cascade region within the full complex achieved 3.5 Å (FSC = 0.143). Free Cascade and Cascade–TniQ populations were resolved to 2.8 Å, 3.0 Å (closed) and 3.1 Å (open), respectively (FSC = 0.143). The HIC exhibits variable local resolution (3.7–9.0 Å, Supplementary Fig. 9), and focused refinements were combined into a composite map.

For the STC maps, PDB 9Y7B was used as a starting model. The structure was initially docked into the STC-without-target-DNA map and manually rebuilt in Coot (v0.9.8.96)54 where required. DNA sequences were modified manually and fitted into the density using ISOLDE as a ChimeraX plugin (v1.11.1). The TnsA subunit was modelled using AlphaFold 3 and docked into the corresponding density. This assembled STC model was subsequently used as the starting model for the STC-with-target-DNA map. Structural rearrangements in TnsB required individual domains to be docked independently into the density before rejoining in Coot.

For the Cascade–TniQ complex structures, individual Cas subunits were modelled using AlphaFold 3 and docked into the map. The DNA scaffold was derived from PDB 6PIJ and mutated to match the designed substrate sequence. The target recognition complex was assembled, and manual adjustments were performed in Coot.

It has been revealed that both the Cascade–TniQ and STC complex structures were used as starting models for modelling the HIC. TnsC protomers were individually modelled using AlphaFold 3 and docked into the density. The STC–TnsC portion of the HIC was used as the starting model for the off-pathway complex, with minor adjustments applied to the TnsC ring.

Recent findings suggest that for all structures, real-space refinement of DNA substrates was performed in Phenix (v2.0rc1-5690)55 with base-pair and secondary structure restraints enforced. Model validation was carried out by computing map-model FSC at a 0.5 cut-off. The masked cross-correlation coefficient (CCmask) from refinement output was reported as the representative model-map cross-correlation. All validation statistics are summarized in Extended Data Table 1.

In a recent development, helical rise and twist were measured from docked protomers in the HIC (PDB: 36AU) and VchTnsC structures (PDB: 7UFI) using a script from the Rosetta software suite: make_symmdef_file.pl56. Rise values (in Å) were extracted from the output and plotted using Python.

Newcastle chiefs are inching closer to confirming a upcoming stadium as their direction of travel.

We reported in last week’s Newcastle Confidential how advanced talks with New York investment bankers Goldman Sachs over financing the £1.3billion project had indicated significant progress on the decision to leave St James’ Park, with a 65,000-capacity stadium on nearby Leazes Park the intention.

Fellow Wall Street firm JP Morgan have now been appointed as advisers in selling a stake in the club, and this would be to inject newly introduced equity to help fund infrastructural developments, including a stadium.

Sources have stressed this is not a case of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund looking to sell the club, but rather by creating fresh shares – potentially worth up to 25 per cent of the club – it raises capital for such a significant outlay.

Recent findings suggest that with Newcastle said to be valued at £1.5billion, this could equate to a £375million cash injection. PIF would retain their majority ownership, even if diluted to around 63 per cent from its current 85 per cent holding.

As one source mentioned: ‘This is not about taking cash off the table, it is about funding growth.'.

Yasir Al-Rummayan and Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund are not looking to sell Newcastle despite their prepares to sell a stake in the club.

According to recent reports, we understand Goldman Sachs are still involved, and their role will be to provide a loan or other investment to help finance the stadium. As we reported last week, the cost of a newly introduced home would not be exclusively funded by PIF and co-owner Jamie Reuben, with loans, share challenges and investments all part of the package.

According to recent reports, the expectation is that a new stadium, rather than a St James’ renovation, will soon be recommended to the club’s owners by the executive team. It will then be up to PIF to sign off on the looks and for a public announcement to be prepared.

REVEALED: What Dedic was doing in bow and arrow fiasco!

Amar Dedic was firing arrows at a tree during his infamous countryside escapade, Confidential can now reveal.

The details of exactly what the Newcastle defender was doing with a bow and arrows in a Northumberland beauty spot can be shared for the first time after police closed the case, including the deployment of a helicopter to track him down.

The chopper was part of a major search operation in which Dedic and his friend were stopped by more than half a dozen patrol cars.

It has been revealed that investigators are now satisfied the 24-year-old posed no threat to the public after a 999 caller reported seeing two men walking by a reservoir with what they described as a ‘crossbow’. It was, in fact, a bow and arrows.

It has been revealed that I can reveal that Dedic was not hunting animals (or the public) during his Harlow Hill adventure, but was instead using a tree for target practice. He and his pal were firing beyond a fence with the aim of landing their arrows in the trunk.

However, while the recreational archers were walking back to Dedic’s car, the emergency call was made by a concerned member of the public. Police cars, including armed response, arrived on the scene but the Bosnian had left.

Amar Dedic was firing arrows at a tree during his infamous countryside escapade, which saw police despatch a helicopter to track him down.

Dedic has taken the misunderstanding in good spirits, and we can expect him to copy Harvey Barnes' archer celebration if he scores in the coming weeks.

This prompted controllers at Northumbria Police HQ to scramble a helicopter to join the hunt and, seven miles away in the exclusive Darras Hall estate, Dedic was pulled over amid a blaze of blue lights.

Sources indicate that adding to the incredulity of the situation was the sudden appearance of goalkeeper Mark Gillespie and former defender Paul Dummett, who helped Dedic and police during questioning. They were in the area by chance.

Dedic has taken the misunderstanding in good spirits and, if he does score his first goal for Newcastle in the coming weeks, we should expect a Harvey Barnes-style archer celebration.

Joelinton is set to return to action next week – in time for the Tyne-Wear derby.

Confidential reported last week that the prognosis was not as bad as first feared after the Brazilian suffered a muscle injury during the defeat by Everton on November 2. However, I’m now told Joelinton is expected to return to full training next week, with Manchester United the visitors on Wednesday followed by the clash with Sunderland four days later.

Sources indicate that the 30-year-old started three league games after a previous injury absence before he broke down again, raising serious questions over his ability to withstand a Premier League season. Nonetheless, Joelinton’s involvement for the derby would be a major boost to Matthias Jaissle in his first taste of the fixture.

First images of Toon's luxury private members' club.

Newcastle have taken inspiration from NFL giants Dallas Cowboys as they explore looks for a luxury private members' club at their £190million training headquarters – and I can reveal stunning images of how the exclusive facility would look.

Confidential understands club chiefs have been studying some of the world's leading sporting complexes, including The Star, the Cowboys' spectacular training base in Texas, as they look to transform their own 260-acre site into a world-class destination.

And their ambitions could extend well beyond football. Newcastle have now approached existing hospitality clients and members of their business club to gauge interest in a private members' retreat within the proposed training complex at Woolsington, which is set to open in the summer of 2029.

We can reveal the first concept images of a private members' club at Newcastle's proposed £190m training base.

The Dallas Cowboys' HQ in Frisco, Texas is one source of inspiration for the envisaged facility at Woolsington (pictured).

Recent findings suggest that the market research includes questions about whether prospective members would be interested in business meeting spaces, a licensed bar and leisure club facilities. The idea is to create an exclusive social and business hub alongside the new training ground, which will house the men's first team and academy, with further plans to integrate the women's team.

Sources indicate that the Dallas Cowboys' headquarters in Frisco, Texas, has provided one source of inspiration. Known as The Star, the sprawling development combines elite training facilities with hospitality, entertainment, restaurants and commercial spaces. Club officials have visited NFL facilities as part of extensive research into how the world's leading sports organisations operate away from matchdays.

The striking concept images that we are able to bring you offer a glimpse of the scale of Newcastle's ambition as they seek to build a complex that will rank as one of the best in world football.

Wilson's familiar latest neighbour.

Sporting director Ross Wilson has a new neighbour – Matthias Jaissle!

The pair are now living in the same complex in the Jesmond area of Newcastle, after Jaissle spent an initial period staying in the Dakota Hotel on the city’s Quayside.

This should prove handy ahead of the January window, and the club’s transfer war room might well become Wilson’s living room!

The car park also offers a clue as to what time Jaissle is starting work every day, and given Wilson rarely sees the manager’s vehicle there in the morning, it is assumed he is at the club’s Benton base before the milkman!

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle is out of the Dakota Hotel, having moved into the same complex as the club's sporting director Ross Wilson.

Finally, Newcastle have beaten Sunderland on Tyneside, 16 years after their last league victory!

Two teams of legends played a game of walking football at Newcastle’s Foundation building close to St James’ Park on Wednesday.

In a recent development, and we can reveal that Newcastle won 14-3! The Toon team included Shay Given, Olivier Bernard, Steve Howey, Shola Ameobi, Dummett, John Anderson and Kenny Wharton. The top scorers, surprisingly, were noted to be former left backs Bernard and Dummett!

The get-together was aimed at raising awareness over walking football opportunities, with the Newcastle Foundation and Sunderland’s Foundation of Light both supporting the sport through various initiatives.

German economy returns to growth, so why is the country still worried?

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1233 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Is Germany's economy back on the up?
  • Recent findings suggest that at the 2026 Mechanical Engineering Summit in Berlin this week, the mood was sullen.
  • Industry observers note that the mechanical and plant engineering sector was the backbone of German industry for decades.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Is Germany's economy back on the up? The answer to that question depends on your perspective.

Recent findings suggest that at the 2026 Mechanical Engineering Summit in Berlin this week, the mood was sullen. "A year ago, I mentioned here: We are angry. Today I must say: We are stunned," Bertram Kawlath, president of the Mechanical Engineering Industry Association (VDMA), said in his opening remarks on Tuesday.

Industry observers note that the mechanical and plant engineering sector was the backbone of German industry for decades. It once employed more than a million people; now 15,000 positions are being cut every month. Production has shrunk about 20% since 2018.

Kawlath criticized the federal government's infighting and lack of reform, as well as what the companies consider a continued high bureaucracy and tax burden.

Sources indicate that "[We are] stunned by the whitewashing in so many government statements. Stunned by the increasingly visible decline of our country as a business location.".

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz promised quick reforms and a rapidly noticeable economic upswing when he took office in May 2025. A year and a half later, reality has caught up with him.

Recent findings suggest that merz's coalition of his conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU), its Bavarian sister party the Christian Social Union, (CSU), along with the center-left Social Democrats(SPD), keeps running into trouble. In addition, there are crises and wars. The German economy is facing more headwinds than seldom before, Merz said in October at the German Employers' Day conference in Berlin.

Sources indicate that given the circumstances, small successes are even more meaningful. "A heartfelt thanks for the good news you bring," Merz said when he received the autumn report of the Council of Economic Experts in Berlin, which predicted economic growth of 1.3% for 2026 and 1% for 2027.

The economic experts have a German government mandate to independently analyze business activity and make recommendations for economic policy. Earlier this year, they were much more pessimistic.

Recent findings suggest that "The German economy has recovered quicker than expected from the energy price shock sparked by the war in Iran," mentioned Monika Schnitzer, chair of the expert advisory board, explaining the prognosis. "We see a significant economic recovery, driven by surprisingly strong exports and high government spending.".

The chancellor, who celebrated his 71st birthday on November 11, spoke of "encouraging signals" in his address. "The economy in Germany is slowly on the rise again. Considering the many crises in Germany, it was not totally expected that we would manage that.".

But these improved prospects do not change the long-term problems. An ageing society means the bills for pensions, health and caregiving are constantly rising.

Industry observers note that at the same time, the number of working-age people who finance these services is sinking. That puts increasing pressure on the public purse. According to Berlin's financial planning, social welfare costs, defense and interest on debt will account for 80% of the spending in the federal government's budget.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"We must realize that in the long term the expected revenues in the federal budget will not be enough to cover the planned expenses," Schnitzer warned. The growth rates are far below what is needed to secure the same level of prosperity as previous decades in the long term.

"To grow out of this budgetary predicament, we would need levels of economic growth which we haven't experienced in Germany for the past 50 years," she remarked.

According to recent reports, the government is presently in final deliberations over its 2027 budget; spending upwards of €555 billion ($615 billion) is planned. Because revenue won't be enough to cover it, the government is planning to take on more than €118 billion in fresh debt. Adding the debt-financed special funds for infrastructure and the military, the new borrowing adds up to almost €204 billion.

In a recent development, the economic experts have warned that if Germany continues with this path, the debt-to-GDP ratio could rise to 100% by 2040. This ratio indicates how high the national debt is in relation to annual economic output. At the end of 2025, it was 63.5%.

According to recent reports, germany is the only country of the world's leading democratic industrialized nations (G7) to still hold a AAA rating, the best possible credit rating in finance markets. It signals to investors the smallest possible default risk for German government bonds. "I want it to stay that way," Merz emphasized.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It has been revealed that however, taking on less debt will not be simple. "A reduction in debt-based financing presents policymakers with a consolidation task of historic proportions and will require tough decisions," noted Schnitzer. The belt-tightening must, however, be designed to enable growth. Some recommendations include reducing environmentally harmful tax benefits — like the energy tax breaks for diesel fuel.

The so-called "mothers' pension", a pension subsidy for older parents, should be revoked, said the experts. Tax increases could become necessary in the medium term, for example with value-added tax.

"The burden should be shared fairly between generations and societal groups," Schnitzer said.

According to the chancellor, the experts' message has been received. Solid state finances are an matter in Germany but also throughout the European Union. Merz remarked there needs to be a consolidation course, adding that politicians have a duty to the younger generation. Reforms are needed, especially when it comes to social security systems.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Economic researchers are setting their hopes on increasing companies' productivity. Put simply, productivity describes how much a manufacturer can generate with its employees, machinery and resources in a set time.

According to the Council of Economic Experts, there is enormous variation even within the same industries. In Germany, the top companies are up to five times as productive as the weakest enterprises.

If the less productive companies caught up, economic growth could increase significantly, it mentioned in the report. "Upcoming technologies and business models could drive peak productivity and allow new highly productive companies to develop.".

But innovations need capital. It's here that the Ifo Economic Research Institute sees considerable deficiencies.

New evaluations show that German universities produce significantly fewer successful business startups than their counterparts in the United Kingdom or United States. For example, for every 1,000 students, about 14 venture capital-backed founders emerge from the vicinity of Stanford University each year. In Cambridge, the European leader, it's 3.5. In Munich, by contrast, it's only 0.5.

There continues to be an abundance of inventors and tinkerers in Germany, especially in mechanical engineering. However, the message from the industry summit in Berlin was that for renewed success, labor costs must come down. Suggestions included longer working hours and more flexibility for employers around job protection.

It has been revealed that the intention was not to cut employees' wages and salaries. However, a newly introduced study by the German Economic Institute commissioned for the German Mechanical Engineering Industry Association revealed that extending the working week by an hour alone would increase real gross domestic product by 1.5% in the coming five years.

This article was originally written in German.

Harry Kane ends England’s 25-year wait for Ballon d’Or winner

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that “Wow, wow, wow,” Harry Kane said as he took to the stage at the London Palladium after winning the 2026 Ballon d’Or.
  • Sources indicate that in truth it would have been a travesty had the 33-year-old England captain – and Bayern Munich striker – not won with his family, friends and coaches all watching from the stalls at this famous old theatre.
  • Kane’s speech was as outstanding as his football.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that “Wow, wow, wow,” Harry Kane said as he took to the stage at the London Palladium after winning the 2026 Ballon d’Or. Wow indeed. “I am speechless,” Kane added before launching into a heartfelt speech, the wobble in his voice showing just how much this meant to him.

Sources indicate that in truth it would have been a travesty had the 33-year-old England captain – and Bayern Munich striker – not won with his family, friends and coaches all watching from the stalls at this famous old theatre. “All those years of sacrifice,” he said of his parents, Pat and Kim, his voice faltering more than ever at that moment. It was from the heart. And faltering again as he spoke about his wife and “best friend” Katie Goodland. “This is a trophy we all celebrate,” he said, talking to his children back in Bavaria. “I bring a few others [trophies] home but this one is a special one.”.

Kane’s speech was as outstanding as his football. “Lastly for me it is the journey,” he said. “Learn through resilience, determination and self-belief. My journey was not easy and I had to fight my way to be the very best right now. I hope that can give you inspiration.”.

So much for the “one-season wonder”. So much for the doubters who poured scorn on him. So much for those who believed he would never make it after loan spells at Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich City and Leicester City. With varying degrees of success.

According to recent reports, kate Scott, the presenter, perfectly detected the emotion and stated: “You held it together. You got through it.” It showed how much it meant to Kane, who simply and quietly replied: “Yes”.

In a recent development, what a winner. What a player. What a role model. The award given in the city where he has scored most of his goals. But he would not have been in the running for this accolade had he not been brave enough to quit Tottenham Hotspur after 19 years and move to Germany.

Kane was the favourite. But, despite its prestige, the Ballon d’Or process is an odd one. One journalist from each of the top-100-ranked Fifa countries is given a vote, with the organisers, France Football, laying out the criteria: individual performance, collective performance and fair play. In that order. They often go for the biggest name. Not the best.

Kane’s numbers are incredible. They speak for themselves. Those numbers show he deserved to win the prize: 65 games for club and country and 73 goals. Plus eight assists (for the judging period – August 3, 2025 to July 19, 2026). That is 61 goals for Bayern and 12 for England. That is a goal less than every 72 minutes. That is beyond elite. That is world class and legendary.

Bayern Munich and England's Ballon d'Or winner doing what he does best 🎯 https://t.co/yWNburqkpg.

It has been revealed that for his club, that is 19 goals more than any other player in the top five European leagues. And the most since Cristiano Ronaldo scored 61 for Real Madrid in 2014-15. Kane won last season’s Golden Shoe by nine goals from Erling Haaland. He reached his century of Bundesliga goals last month in just 98 games, destroying Dieter Müller’s record set 49 years ago – he took 129 matches.

Kane became one of only two players in history (the other is Ronaldo) to score 20-plus goals across World Cups and European Championships and was the only one to score in two major club cup finals, including a hat-trick. Neither Kylian Mbappé nor Lamine Yamal, his closest rivals, scored in any finals.

Both gave interviews declaring why they should win the Ballon d’Or. Kane? “I don’t like talking about myself,” he mentioned. “The 73 goals speak for themselves.” They do.

Those are the facts, but there is also the football and, yes, the conduct. Kane has scored some superb goals during that period, not least for England. Take his two goals against the Democratic Republic of Congo at the World Cup that saved his team and Thomas Tuchel from an embarrassing early exit.

The Prince of Wales, who has been FA president since 2006, congratulated Kane on “a fantastic achievement”.

“A brilliant captain, a remarkable player and someone who has given football fans across the world so many unforgettable moments,” Prince William wrote on Instagram.

Kane, the first English player since Michael Owen in 2001 to win the award, is also the ultimate team player – so fulfilling that “collective performance” criteria – and a captain who leads by example on and off the pitch. Fair play? He was last booked in January and was cautioned just three times in 68 games and not at all in any of his 13 appearances this season.

And he works hard, so very hard. Kane was in the top 10 for total distance covered at the World Cup, despite playing a game fewer than most of the others on the list. And he is often seen winning as many defensive headers in his own penalty area as attacking ones in the opposition’s.

That work extends to off the pitch, to try to maximise his ability, to do everything to be the best version of himself and to be the best. Which he has now been recognised as. And it stems from his winning mentality. Some scoffed when Kane walked into England’s press conference before the 2018 World Cup and stated he could be top-scorer – but he proved them wrong.

They probably also scoffed at the notion that he would one day be declared the best player in the world and win the Ballon d’Or. But he has done all that. It confirms England’s all-time cap holder (for now jointly with Peter Shilton) and goalscorer as one of the greats. And we are privileged to witness that greatness. Wow, what a night.

By Christian FalkGermany do not have a single player among the 30 in the running to win the Ballon d’Or in London on Monday night – but Bayern Munich do have England captain Harry Kane.

Sources indicate that for the 35-time German champions, the award is perhaps even more notable than it is for the peerless striker himself. The Bayern hierarchy are planning to travel to the Palladium Theatre en masse to support Kane.

In a recent development, kane is not only Bayern’s top striker, he is their international figurehead and, internally, their poster-boy professional. Club patron and honorary president Uli Hoeness described the England captain as the best signing in the club’s history. Hoeness even went so far as to say he loves Kane, and he is not alone in this.

There's only one Harry Kane. https://t.co/NfZEFmjaUN.

Hoeness is one of many in the club’s leadership who have been endlessly promoting Kane to help the 33-year-old fulfil his lifelong dream of winning the trophy. Bayern officials have been campaigning on his behalf for weeks.

First up was manager Vincent Kompany, who remains in hospital for tests after collapsing at Bayern’s training ground on Friday. Kompany said: “If he can now crown his career or his season with the Ballon d’Or, that would be fitting given the way he plays for the team.”.

Sources indicate that the plaudits kept coming. Whether it was sporting director Max Eberl (“He has more than earned the Ballon d’Or. Anyone who loves football loves characters like Harry Kane”), chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen (“One thing is clear – anyone talking about this year’s greatest individual honours cannot overlook Harry Kane”) or president Herbert Hainer (“Harry Kane embodies the idea that sporting greatness is incomplete without greatness of character. He would be a worthy World Footballer of the Year”), everyone at the club is fighting for Kane.

The official Ballon d’Or website has announced Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal as winners of the main prize in an embarrassing blunder for the organisation.

Three separate articles were published before quickly being taken down.

The headline on Kane’s article read: ‘Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d’Or: Here are his best and most meaningful strikes from a 61-goal season’.

The 70th Ballon d’Or ceremony takes place at the London Palladium as England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane aims to become the first Englishman in more than 20 years to win the award. Michael Owen was the last Englishman to win the award back in 2001.

The choice of London as the host city pays tribute to the award’s inaugural winner, England’s Stanley Matthews, who won it in 1956. This also marks the first time the ceremony will be organised outside France. Kane, who scored over 70 goals for club and country in the relevant year, is among the favourites for this year’s award alongside the likes of Barcelona and Spain’s Lamine Yamal and Real Madrid and France’s Kylian Mbappe.

According to recent reports, kane won the Bundesliga with Bayern Munich whereas Yamal won both La Liga and the World Cup. Yamal won the Kopa Trophy at last year’s ceremony as the best men’s young player.

Industry observers note that last year’s winners were Spain and Barcelona midfielder Aitana Bonmati and France and Barcelona forward Ousmane Dembele. Dembele is aiming to become just the 11th man to win the top prize at least twice, although it would appear to be very unlikely that the Frenchman will be winning the award this evening.

Sources indicate that selected international journalists cast their votes based on the performances of players throughout the season. The panel consists of one representative per country from the top 100 nations in the Fifa men’s world ranking and the top 50 in the women’s world ranking. Each voter ranks their top 10 candidates, with points distributed on a descending scale. They vote based on three factors: individual performance, team achievements, and class combined with fair play.

In total, 13 trophies will be presented across the men’s and women’s game, including the two man Ballon d’Or awards, the best young players and best teams. The awards take into account achievements from August 3, 2025, to July 19, 2026 (August 16 for the women).

The official ceremony begins at 8pm GMT.

Latest Update: AI in classrooms: Fighting the great 'dumbing down'

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1411 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Jakob is 15 years old and attends a secondary school for more academic students, known in Germany as a gymnasium.
  • "I had a French test today, and yesterday I had ChatGPT explain a lot of the topics to me again," the student told DW.
  • Math, German, English, chemistry and even physics: In one click, the solution or the path to a solution is available thanks to AI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jakob is 15 years old and attends a secondary school for more academic students, known in Germany as a gymnasium. He and his classmates have already been using artificial intelligence-enabled tools, or AI, for the last two and a half years.

"I had a French test today, and yesterday I had ChatGPT explain a lot of the topics to me again," the student told DW. Jakob isn't his real name, because he doesn't want to publicly admit he and many others of his age use AI to do their homework.

Math, German, English, chemistry and even physics: In one click, the solution or the path to a solution is available thanks to AI.

In science, this is called "cognitive outsourcing." Basically, the required thinking is shifted to another device, whether that's a calculator, notepad or a large language model (LLM) like ChatGPT.

There's a difference with AI, though. A notepad or calculator can take over a step or two but rarely the whole thought process. That's not the same for an LLM, which can handle the entire problem-solving process.

Sources indicate that jakob admitted he's also had an AI help him with his homework. "But only when I was really stuck," he insisted. And he's also aware that it can become a problem when AI does all your homework. "The students who get good grades tend not to do that," he explained.

Franziska Müller has been a German teacher for several decades and is currently teaching senior classes at a gymnasium. Her name has also been changed for privacy reasons.

"They can't even think for themselves anymore," she told DW, complaining about some of her classes.

Even in ordinary classes, some of the students type their questions into their tablets or phones, asking for AI assistance. And should they be called upon in class, she knows that they're reading out the answers that the AI has prepared for them and hoping nobody notices.

Müller believes students these days are less able to comprehend text. "Because they read less and let AI summarize almost everything for them," she mentioned.

Several studies have reached very similar conclusions.

That includes the latest PISA (Program for International Student Assessment) study from September. PISA, which is run by the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development, regularly evaluates the abilities of 15-year-old students around the world.

"Students who report using AI chatbots get lower scores in science, on average, than those who don't use AI," Andreas Schleicher, the OECD director for education and skills, wrote in his report in October. "This includes using AI to summarize texts they had to read, conduct preliminary research on a latest topic, or draft texts for writing assignments.".

With participants from more than 90 countries, PISA is considered the largest international comparative study of 15-year-olds worldwide. This year, German 15-year-olds posted their lowest PISA scores in the 25-year history of the study.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"The connections are complex and depend heavily on how generative AI is used, but the central insight is simple: Just as we don't get fit by watching sports but by doing sports ourselves, learning doesn't come from consuming content, but from the mind's productive cognitive engagement with new material," Schleicher explained.

Put simply, those who don't exercise their brains risk becoming less intelligent.

US think tank, the Brookings Institution, has already argued that the risks of using AI in education outweigh the benefits.

Its own research, which included young participants from around the world, speaks of students losing "fundamental cognitive and durable skills as they increasingly rely on AI to perform learning's intellectual work," as well as the decline of critical thinking, memory, perseverance and independent judgment.

But what can be done against the power of ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, Gemini and Meta AI?

New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani has banned the use of AI in public schools up to the eighth grade for the 2026 and 2027 school years — so that's up to about the age of 14 or 15.

In a recent development, not everyone agrees this is the right thing to do. Julian Hinn, who teaches German to students aged between 15 and 18 in Germany, said class members can still use AI apps on their mobile phones. "And anyone who thinks they won't use it at home is ignoring reality," Hinn told DW.

Germany's annual JIM study, which tracks teenagers' media use and device ownership, supports that view.

Industry observers note that 91% of young people surveyed in Germany, between the ages of 12 and 19, stated that they use at least one AI application. The study also reports that 74% use AI for homework and learning.

It has been revealed that the last JIM study actually dates back to 2024 so those percentages might be even higher now. Data on AI use in Asia, Latin America and the US from the Brookings study show similarly high figures.

Sources indicate that german politicians have recognized the problem. Although education in Germany is the responsibility of the individual federal states, the so-called Standing Conference of the Ministers of Education and Cultural Affairs, or KMK, has been issuing statements on the use of AI since 2024.

The KMK's statements have been rather vague though, saying only that students should be enabled to engage with AI in a critical, reflective and responsible manner.

Teachers and students alike are aware that AI can be a powerful support in the classroom.

"The AIs simply explain things much better than textbooks," noted Jakob, adding that he'll often get an AI to explain basic concepts to him.

Recent findings suggest that sometimes teachers can't respond like an AI, Hinn conceded. "The AI ​​can respond much better to the language and needs of the students.".

It has been revealed that that's why he thinks it's crucial to include AI in classes, starting from the 10th grade when students are around 15 or 16. Hinn doesn't think it should be introduced before that, when children's basic skills are still being developed.

In more senior classes, Hinn will encourage his students to question the AI critically. "We look at the quality of the solutions," he explained.

Industry observers note that german teacher Müller has also integrated some use of AI into her lessons for older students. But in some aspects of the class, she also bans it altogether so that her students can focus on thinking for themselves.

"I understand very well that it's tempting to use AI," she mentioned.

Sources indicate that there are also other problems with AI in education. According to the Brookings study, students with basic skills can use AI to deepen their learning and progress faster.

Industry observers note that but for children with gaps in their knowledge, they tend to adopt AI's errors, outsource their thinking and then fall even further behind. In this way, AI can exacerbate preexisting inequalities.

The PISA study notes that children from more affluent backgrounds often have a better start, and AI can widen that gap.

This is called the Matthew effect — the name comes from the biblical verse Matthew 25:29, "for unto everyone that hath shall be given." It basically means that early success in learning leads to better progress in the future, while early struggles equal a growing lag over time.

In the age of AI, teachers have become more motivated to challenge students to think independently and to consider their own personal autonomy.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Hinn, who also supervises the school newspaper, said: "I always tell everyone, you can use AI but the feeling of having written an article with your own pen is spectacular.".

Sources indicate that both teachers also stress the idea of personal autonomy and responsibility. They believe this affects the students, especially because when they sit exams, they aren't allowed to use any aids or AI. And if they aren't able to solve their own problems, they will fail.

It's during exam time that the students really find out if they can solve those math, English or science problems by themselves.

Müller remarked one of her students recently confessed they were upset after a poor exam result. "He felt he simply couldn't think for himself anymore because of AI," she said.

This article was originally written in German.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Roma and Paris Saint-Germain attacker Javier Pastore has shared his thoughts ahead of the meeting of his two former clubs in the Champions League on Wednesday evening, and has explained what makes the two teams so enjoyable to watch: ‘Gasperini has made his philosophy clear to the players, like Lucho at PSG’.

Industry observers note that roma face another tough test in the Champions League away against the reigning champions, PSG, on Wednesday night. The Giallorossi have four points from their opening four matches in the competition this season after tests away against Fenerbahce and Manchester United and at home against Slovan Bratislava and Real Madrid.

Sources indicate that PSG, meanwhile, have had a perfect start and will be looking to make it five wins from five on Wednesday night. Luis Enrique’s side have beaten Slovan Bratislava, Manchester City, Barcelona and Villarreal already this season.

“Both play to impose themselves with great talents in attack,” said Pastore in an interview with La Gazzetta dello Sport. “They have coaches who work differently, but with the same attacking and counter-attacking principles. PSG will be more confident and have a perfect record, Roma need to pick up points. It will be an exciting game.”.

Pastore feels that the coaches might be both sides’ strongest assets.

Sources indicate that “Both know how to get into their players’ heads. They are not just good tactically, but also at managing their teams, which is fundamental in modern football. I don’t know Gasperini very well, but he did great things at Atalanta and he’s brought an offensive, selfless style of play to Roma. They take risks and have lots of quality going forwards.

“He’s made his philosophy clear to the players, like Lucho at PSG, where he has changed the game concepts and the players’ mentality, who still follow him after winning two Champions Leagues.”.

Pastore pinpointed the players that Roma should be wary of.

Sources indicate that “I’ve always liked Doue and Kvaratskhelia, who won’t be involved unfortunately, but also Mendes and Hakimi, the best full-backs in the world. I also like everything about Neves, a very special player who doesn’t always draw attention, but always helps his team in recovery, building from the back, creating space, looking for smart passes and arriving in front of goal. He’s a complete player.”.

Industry observers note that “For Roma, Dybala is a spectacle, dangerous anywhere. Malen is better than any other striker this year. And there’s also Soule, who brings something different, is technical and dribbles and scores well.”.

Alarmingly for Roma, Pastore indicates that there are no weaknesses in the PSG side.

Industry observers note that “I don’t see any, but maybe they will come out while the game is in progress. PSG are a united team built on the consistency of their play both in attack and defence. And Gasperini is following a similar path with Roma, always wanting to score one more than the opponent. You could even see it against Real Madrid, despite the result.”.

Still, Malen’s form is encouraging. The Dutchman has scored 16 goals from 15 games across all competitions and netted four goals during Roma’s 5-1 win over Parma on Sunday.

“With Malen in this type of form, pretty much any ball into the box ends with a goal and it’s hard to stop him. Dybala is dangerous in every situation: From free-kicks, from the edge of the area, with an assist or a shot into the top corner. These are the types of players who usually give you something extra in games like this.”.

And lastly, when asked if he had to pick a side, Pastore mentioned: “Rome is beautiful with wonderful people, a place I lived for three great years. I’m in Paris more often because I got married there, and my children were born there. But I would take the Italian food anywhere.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Everton in the Community (EitC) supported more than 46,400 people through its programmes during the 2025/26 season – an increase of almost 10,000 on the previous year – according to the charity's latest Impact Report, which also highlights its £80.1 million annual social value. Dedicated to breaking down barriers and tackling social inequality since 1988, the charitable arm of Everton Football Club supports some of the most vulnerable and underrepresented members of its local community. Through more than 50 evidence-based, inclusive programmes, EitC addresses health inequalities, creates pathways into education and employment, and tackles crime and anti-social behaviour. Its work continues to evolve in response to local needs. During the 2025/26 season alone, Everton in the Community supported 46,463 people while more than 156,000 individuals were reached through wider community engagement activity. As Everton Football Club moved to Hill Dickinson Stadium at the start of the season, EitC made a conscious decision to remain rooted in L4, protecting Goodison Park's community legacy while continuing to invest in one of England's most deprived neighbourhoods. The charity’s mission continued to be shaped by the Trinity Project, its five-year strategy to ‘create stronger communities and brighter futures’ for all through three key pillars designed to drive lasting change: Minds, Learns and Thrives. Speaking about the latest Impact Report, Chief Executive Officer of Everton in the Community, Sue Gregory noted: “Every year, this report provides an opportunity to reflect on what we have achieved together, and once again, I am incredibly proud of the difference our charity has made to tens of thousands of lives across Liverpool City Region. “At Everton in the Community, we believe football has the power to do far more than just entertain. It has the ability to inspire, connect people, tackle inequality and create lasting change.” More than half of children in Liverpool live in income-deprived families, compared with 38% nationally, while the cost-of-living crisis continues to place increasing pressure on local households and contribute to food insecurity. Everton in the Community supported 1,293 people experiencing poverty, providing access to food, housing and debt advice, alongside high-quality, discounted food through its weekly Blue Base Pantry. Health inequalities remain a significant challenge across Liverpool City Region, with local communities experiencing some of the poorest health outcomes and highest levels of poor mental health in the country. EitC is working to address these inequalities by bringing vital healthcare services directly into trusted community settings, helping people access support and identify health concerns earlier. One example highlighted in the latest Impact Report is the award-winning BEAT Breathlessness Hub, which last season alone provided more than 900 people with access to heart and lung screenings and helped reduce the clinical pathway for heart failure from six months to one hour. Mental health support also remained a key priority, with EitC supporting more than 9,000 people across the Liverpool City Region during the season and engaging 1,215 supporters through its ‘Together Against Suicide’ matchday support service. The charity also helped tackle social isolation by providing weekly social activities for 217 older residents and supported people living with dementia and their carers through its ‘Pass on the Memories’ programme. Educational inequality remains a significant challenge across Merseyside. Seven of the 20 constituencies in the country with the highest levels of special educational needs among children are in the region, with Liverpool Walton recording the highest percentage nationally. In parts of North Liverpool, almost a third of the working-age population also have no formal qualifications. EitC works to remove barriers and widen pathways into education, training and employment for people of all ages – supporting children from their earliest years through to young people and adults preparing for future careers. During the 2025/26 season, 16,583 people were supported on their educational journey, including 488 children who were helped to achieve their Early Learning Goals. The charity also supported more than 2,500 young people identified as being at risk of becoming NEET, while helping 90 people move into employment and 13 into apprenticeships. Speaking about the future, Sue continued: “We know that the landscape around us continues to change. “Financial pressures, inequality, poverty, poor mental health and barriers to education and employment are placing increasing demands on communities and the organisations supporting them. This makes our role more notable than ever. “None of this would be possible without our incredible staff, volunteers, participants, partners, donors and supporters. Together, we have built something truly special. “The next chapter is only just the beginning, and I am incredibly excited about what we can achieve together.” To read the latest Impact Report in full, click here. For more information about Everton in the Community’s 50+ programmes, visit our website here.

Everton in the Community (EitC) supported more than 46,400 people through its programmes during the 2025/26 season – an increase of almost 10,000 on the previous year – according to the charity's latest Impact Report, which also highlights its £80.1 million annual social value.

Dedicated to breaking down barriers and tackling social inequality since 1988, the charitable arm of Everton Football Club supports some of the most vulnerable and underrepresented members of its local community.

Through more than 50 evidence-based, inclusive programmes, EitC addresses health inequalities, creates pathways into education and employment, and tackles crime and anti-social behaviour. Its work continues to evolve in response to local needs.

During the 2025/26 season alone, Everton in the Community supported 46,463 people while more than 156,000 individuals were reached through wider community engagement activity.

As Everton Football Club moved to Hill Dickinson Stadium at the start of the season, EitC made a conscious decision to remain rooted in L4, protecting Goodison Park's community legacy while continuing to invest in one of England's most deprived neighbourhoods.

The charity’s mission continued to be shaped by the Trinity Project, its five-year strategy to ‘create stronger communities and brighter futures’ for all through three key pillars designed to drive lasting change: Minds, Learns and Thrives.

Speaking about the latest Impact Report, Chief Executive Officer of Everton in the Community, Sue Gregory said: “Every year, this report provides an opportunity to reflect on what we have achieved together, and once again, I am incredibly proud of the difference our charity has made to tens of thousands of lives across Liverpool City Region.

“At Everton in the Community, we believe football has the power to do far more than just entertain. It has the ability to inspire, connect people, tackle inequality and create lasting change.”.

More than half of children in Liverpool live in income-deprived families, compared with 38% nationally, while the cost-of-living crisis continues to place increasing pressure on local households and contribute to food insecurity.

Everton in the Community supported 1,293 people experiencing poverty, providing access to food, housing and debt advice, alongside high-quality, discounted food through its weekly Blue Base Pantry.

Health inequalities remain a significant challenge across Liverpool City Region, with local communities experiencing some of the poorest health outcomes and highest levels of poor mental health in the country.

EitC is working to address these inequalities by bringing vital healthcare services directly into trusted community settings, helping people access support and identify health concerns earlier.

One example highlighted in the latest Impact Report is the award-winning BEAT Breathlessness Hub, which last season alone provided more than 900 people with access to heart and lung screenings and helped reduce the clinical pathway for heart failure from six months to one hour.

Mental health support also remained a key priority, with EitC supporting more than 9,000 people across the Liverpool City Region during the season and engaging 1,215 supporters through its ‘Together Against Suicide’ matchday support service.

The charity also helped tackle social isolation by providing weekly social activities for 217 older residents and supported people living with dementia and their carers through its ‘Pass on the Memories’ programme.

Educational inequality remains a significant challenge across Merseyside. Seven of the 20 constituencies in the country with the highest levels of special educational needs among children are in the region, with Liverpool Walton recording the highest percentage nationally. In parts of North Liverpool, almost a third of the working-age population also have no formal qualifications.

EitC works to remove barriers and widen pathways into education, training and employment for people of all ages – supporting children from their earliest years through to young people and adults preparing for future careers.

During the 2025/26 season, 16,583 people were supported on their educational journey, including 488 children who were helped to achieve their Early Learning Goals.

The charity also supported more than 2,500 young people identified as being at risk of becoming NEET, while helping 90 people move into employment and 13 into apprenticeships.

Speaking about the future, Sue continued: “We know that the landscape around us continues to change.

In a recent development, “Financial pressures, inequality, poverty, poor mental health and barriers to education and employment are placing increasing demands on communities and the organisations supporting them. This makes our role more crucial than ever.

It has been revealed that “None of this would be possible without our incredible staff, volunteers, participants, partners, donors and supporters. Together, we have built something truly special.

“The next chapter is only just the beginning, and I am incredibly excited about what we can achieve together.”.
